notes:
HubSpot Ticket 77812 — Customer latency escalation summary (ForesightCX)

Account context
- Current usage: Redwood Hosted API in production for support-agent + summarization; evaluating move to Dedicated (VPC) for predictable tail latency + isolation.
- Workload shape: bursty arrivals (queue flushes, ticket storms), mixed context lengths (short chat + long KB extracts), streaming enabled.
- Customer quote (from 2025-03-01 PoC check-in): “Median looks fine, but our customer SLAs get hit when p99 spikes during bursts. We can’t explain it internally.”

Impact statement (what happened)
- Symptom: intermittent burst-driven p99/p999 latency spikes + a smaller number of timeouts during peak periods.
- Blast radius: primarily their US traffic; concentrated on a subset of routes using long-context prompts.
- Business impact as reported:
  - Support-agent sessions degraded (agent wait times), some requests retried (cost blow-up concerns).
  - Escalated to their leadership + procurement stakeholders; tail latency stability is now a go/no-go item for Dedicated.

Timeline (high-level)
- 2025-02-11: Internal postmortem PM-2025-02-11 opened after a broader burst tail-latency event; early signal points to KV cache fragmentation + allocator churn under mixed sequence lengths.
- 2025-02-18: Ticket 77812 opened in HubSpot after ForesightCX escalates latency spikes; request for RCA + mitigation guidance.
- 2025-02-19 to 2025-02-21: Support/SRE triage + mitigation guidance shared (temporary limits/admission control tuning; routing to reduce long-context concentration).
- 2025-02-24: Dedicated evaluation call; Redwood commits to a compaction-focused fix with a canary plan and explicit rollback criteria.
- 2025-03-01: PoC check-in (Fireflies ff-2025-03-01-poc-checkin-latency-stability). Customer provides burst traces; Redwood shares draft canary checklist and proposed metrics.
- 2025-03-04: Risk review with infra leadership (Gmail thread-1a77b0c2-canary-risk-review): request for alert thresholds + oncall coverage plan.

Technical summary (current understanding)
- Working hypothesis: KV cache fragmentation under bursty traffic causes allocator overhead + higher probability of expensive re-allocation; triggers tail latency spikes and increases OOM risk in worst mixes.
- Contributing factors we’ve discussed with the customer (no code-level details):
  - Prefill/decode interleaving + uneven block utilization
  - Multi-tenant pool pressure during peak
  - Long-context prompts increasing KV footprint variance

Customer-facing commitments / promised follow-ups
1) Provide written summary suitable for their internal stakeholders
- Scope: plain-English explanation of why tail latency can spike under burst + mixed lengths, and what we’re changing (allocator compaction + scheduler-aware eviction).
- Owner: Lauren Bishop (account) + Sean Gallagher (SRE) for operational details.
- ETA: by end of week after canary start (target: within 5 business days).

2) Mitigation guidance while fix rolls out
- Continue recommended guardrails during peaks (rate limiting on the noisiest routes, conservative max context on the worst offenders, temporary admission control adjustments per pool).
- Confirmed: no breaking API changes; mitigations are configuration-only.

3) Canary plan + explicit success / rollback criteria
- Canary target: one dedicated pool used for PoC traffic (customer-approved), plus one hosted region canary (internal) before broader rollout.
- Success criteria (customer-visible):
  - p99 latency reduction during burst scenario vs current baseline (target: meaningful reduction; we’ll report absolute/relative deltas)
  - allocator allocation failures approach zero under representative load
  - no material regression to median latency
- Rollback criteria:
  - sustained p99 regression above agreed threshold
  - increased allocator failures / OOM signals
  - compaction cost exceeding budget (causing throughput loss)

Mapping to Jira (support) + Engineering rollout milestones
Support tickets
- SUP-4391: Dedicated customer reports bursty p99 spikes; investigation links to KV cache fragmentation; used as primary customer reproduction reference.
- SUP-4410: Hosted API timeouts during high load; support requested interim mitigation guidance; ties into same fragmentation/allocator pressure signals.
- SUP-4422: OOM events correlated with long-context traffic; logs show memory pressure patterns consistent with fragmentation/churn.

Engineering project milestones (for internal tracking / customer comms alignment)
- ENG-2842 (Instrumentation): add fragmentation ratio + allocation failure counters by region/pool/model.
- ENG-2843 (Perf suite): add bursty-mix benchmark; publish baseline + regression gates.
- ENG-2844/2845 (Allocator + eviction): block map abstraction + eviction policy v1.
- ENG-2847 (Triggers/budgets): threshold-based compaction + budget enforcement to protect median latency.
- ENG-2848 (Feature flag): compaction default off; safe toggles for canary/rollback.
- ENG-2851/2852 (Canary + staged rollout): canary in one region + one dedicated pool; expand to 25% with monitoring checklist.
- ENG-2854 (Perf-canary): add gating on p99 + allocator failure rate.

Comms notes (how we’re positioning it)
- Message: “Stability improvement” (tail latency + reduced allocator churn). No behavior change, no prompt/model changes, no customer action required beyond optionally opting into the canary.
- Avoid: over-promising universal p99 improvements across every model + context distribution; commit to reporting their workload’s before/after.

Open questions / asks from customer (captured)
- Do we support VPC deployment with KMS/HSM integration and audit logs? (Answer: yes; provide security FAQ + logging retention details.)
- Can we pin model versions during rollout? (Answer: yes; canary policy will keep model constant; only runtime flag changes.)
- Can they get a weekly update until rollout completes? (Answer: yes; owner to send every Friday during canary/expansion.)

Internal follow-ups
- Ensure KV cache health dashboard panels/alerts are available for the canary window and shared with SE/CSM.
- Confirm oncall coverage plan during the first 24h canary (paging threshold + rollback operator).
- After canary: share a short “what changed / what we measured” note tied to SUP-4391 and Ticket 77812 for audit trail.
